messages.author: df00e1673233d87a
messages.subject: Test for latent mean differences
parts:
Dear lavaan discussion group,

I want to test for latent mean differences as, for example, in this paper (http://www.biomedcentral.com/1471-2288/11/74#). Im am however uncertain about how to specify a test for latent mean differences using lavaan syntax.

So, how do you test for latent mean differences using lavaan?

Best regards,

Johannes Beller

messages.author: 5d4f9e7f97c21008
messages.subject: Re: Test for latent mean differences
parts:
You would want to test latent mean differences using invariance testing. This can be accomplished with the group.equal option in the cfa/sem/lavaan functions in lavaan. Or the process is automated in the measurementInvariance function in the package semTools.

-Alex

I use 'group.equal' option in the cfa functions in lavaan. The presentation material from Kate Xu in the lavaan.org webpage is very helpful to me.

I would like to ask you the possible usage of 'group.equal' option in the sem function, which is specifically related to "regressions". What is 'the practical implications' of group.equal=c("regressions")? It does not seem to provide any interpretative power for the latent variable mean difference. How is it related to the degree of invariance in measurementInvariance function in the semTools? Thank you in advance.

wishes,

Jong-Hwa

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: Test for latent mean differences
parts:
> I would like to ask you the possible usage of 'group.equal' option in
> the sem function, which is specifically related to "regressions". What
> is 'the practical implications' of group.equal=c("regressions")?

This is only relevant if you regressions in your model. It would be
useful, say, in a path analysis setting, and you wish to set all the
paths equal across groups.

> mean difference. How is it related to the degree of invariance in
> measurementInvariance function in the semTools? Thank you in advance.

The group.equal=c("regressions") option is never used in the
measurementInvariance() function.

Yves.

messages.author: 6221508b504c7427
messages.subject: Re: Test for latent mean differences
parts:
When I read cfa.Rd in lavaan with '>?cfa' , I see 'regressions' option in group.equal arguments for cfa(). I think that you would get rid of 'regressions' from group.equal in cfa(), while it should be remain in sem(). This is a minor documentation issue. :)

I think, also, there are some practical confusions on so-called, 'structure invariance' in AMOS manuals. I rather would like to see something like, structureInvariance(), with current measurementInvariance() in lavaan or semTools.

regards,

Jong-Hwa

Thank you very much.
 
Yeah, equal.group=c("regressions") can be used for MIMIC (CFA + covariates) with cfa()!. Sorry for my incautious comment.
 
my question on structure invariance is related to the model with the picture. I was wondering whether my lavaan style syntax below well reflects the picture or not.
 
lat.var1 =~ obs.var1 + obs.var2
lat.var2 =~ obs.var3 + obs.var4
obs.var5 ~ lat.var1 + lat.var2
obs.var6 ~ lat.var1 + lat.var2 + obs.var5
 
Thank you in advance.
 
best regards,
 
Jong-Hwa
